facts.text: Des Allemands translates from French as 'of the Germans,' reflecting its origins as a German immigrant settlement.
Before the Civil War, a railroad depot opened in 1856, and the town’s post office began operating in 1868, later renamed Des Allemands in 1964.
Des Allemands hosts an annual Catfish Festival featuring live music, carnival attractions, and catfish‑based recipes, a tradition started by Reverend William McCallion.
Gertrude Catholic Church, founded in 1901, and public schools dating to 1879 illustrate the town’s Cajun and German‑influenced heritage.
The town lies along Bayou des Allemands, the natural boundary separating Lafourche and St. Charles Parishes.
Des Allemands originated as part of the German Coast, a 18th‑century settlement of German immigrants along the Mississippi River.
